title: Blocking others from Allah's way empties your own deeds.
subtitle: Deeds that come to nothing
then: This surah came in Madinah when the small community was hemmed in by enemies. It opens on those who rejected Allah and {trap}blocked others from His path.{/trap} Ibn Kathir says Allah makes their deeds futile and denies them any reward, {trap}like dust scattered in the air.{/trap}
now: Your friend wants to start praying and you joke about it until she stops. Your colleague wants to give charity and you talk him out of it. {trap}Getting in someone else's way is its own deed.{/trap} {idea}Be the person who opens the door, not the one who blocks it.{/idea}
old: What others do with their faith is not affected by me.
new: If I block someone from good, I lose more than they do.
try: Encourage one person today in a good thing they are trying to do.

title: He wipes away their sins and sets their affairs right.
subtitle: The surah where Muhammad ﷺ is named
then: The surah takes its name from this verse, which names Muhammad ﷺ. Ibn Kathir explains Bal as {reward}their matter, their affair, their condition.{/reward} He notes the Prophet ﷺ taught the reply to one who sneezes: {idea}may Allah guide you and set your affairs right.{/idea}
now: Your life feels tangled: the job, the debt, the family tension, the thing you keep doing that you hate. {reward}The promise here is not just a clean record but a sorted life.{/reward} Belief and good deeds are the first thread to pull.
old: Faith might clean my record, but my life stays messy.
new: Allah promises to set my whole condition right when I believe and do good.
try: When someone sneezes today and praises Allah, reply with may Allah guide you and set your affairs right.

title: The difference is what each side chose to follow.
subtitle: Falsehood or truth from their Lord
then: This verse explains the two before it. Ibn Kathir says deeds are lost for one group and sins forgiven for the other {idea}because one chose falsehood over truth, and the other followed the truth from their Lord.{/idea} Allah makes the end of each path clear.
now: Every day you pick what to follow: which voice in your feed, which friend's advice, which inner urge. {idea}It does not feel like a big decision.{/idea} But the verse says outcomes come from the thing you keep following.
old: Where people end up is mostly chance.
new: Where I end up depends on what I choose to follow, and Allah has made both paths clear.
try: List three voices you follow most. Ask of each: does this lead me to truth?

title: He could have done it Himself; He tests you through each other.
subtitle: Rules for a besieged community, and a deeper purpose
then: The surah introduction says fighting had been ordered for a tiny, boycotted Madinah facing all of Arabia. The verse gives battle guidance, including freeing captives by grace or ransom. {idea}Allah could have punished the enemy Himself, but He lets people be tested by each other.{/idea} {reward}Those killed in His cause will never have their deeds lost.{/reward}
now: The difficult manager. The relative who tests your patience every visit. You wonder why Allah does not just fix it. {idea}The verse says some of us are tested through others.{/idea} How you act in that friction is the point.
old: If Allah wanted, He would just remove the hard people from my life.
new: Allah could remove every difficulty, but some are there to test and grow me.
try: Think of one person who tests you. Choose one calm response before you see them next.

title: Guided onward and their condition set right.
subtitle: What Allah does for those who gave their lives
then: Many believers would die in the coming battles. Ibn Kathir says Allah would multiply their deeds, and that {reward}He will guide them means He will guide them to Paradise.{/reward} {idea}Their situation and affairs will be set right.{/idea}
now: You sit with a family who lost someone good: a nurse who worked through the pandemic, a father who died working to feed his kids. It looks like an ending. {reward}The verse says for those who die striving for Allah, the story keeps going.{/reward}
old: When a good person dies young, it is simply a loss.
new: For those who give themselves for Allah, death opens onto guidance and repair.
try: Make dua today for one good person you know who has passed away.

title: A Paradise He has already made known to them.
subtitle: Not a strange place, but a known one
then: This finishes the promise to those who died in Allah's cause. {reward}He admits them to Paradise, which He has made known to them.{/reward} Ibn Kathir explains it as a place Allah has acquainted them with. {idea}They arrive somewhere they recognize.{/idea}
now: Walking into your childhood home after years abroad: you know where the light switch is without looking. {reward}The verse describes Paradise like that for the believer: not a stranger's place, but one made known.{/reward}
old: Paradise is a far, unknown place I cannot picture.
new: Allah makes Paradise known to its people, so it feels like home.
try: Read one verse describing Paradise today and picture it as a home being prepared.

title: Support Allah's cause and He steadies your feet.
subtitle: Help that comes back to the helper
then: The believers in Madinah were few, poor, and surrounded, as the surah introduction describes. {idea}They are told: if you support Allah's cause, He will support you.{/idea} {reward}He will make your feet firm{/reward}, which is what a frightened, outnumbered group needs most.
now: You stand up for what is right in a meeting and your voice shakes. You keep praying through a stressful exam season. {reward}The verse says the steadiness comes after you take the step.{/reward} Your feet get firmer while you are standing.
old: I need to feel strong before I can stand up for what is right.
new: When I stand for Allah's cause, He gives me the steadiness I lacked.
try: Do one small right thing today that makes you a little nervous, and ask Allah to steady you.

title: For the rejecters, stumbling, and deeds that come to nothing.
subtitle: The opposite of firm feet
then: Right after the promise of firm feet comes its opposite. {trap}For those who disbelieve there is misery, and Allah makes their deeds vain.{/trap} The same pairing as the surah's opening: {idea}what you build on decides whether it lasts.{/idea}
now: You pour years into a goal with no thought of Allah: the house, the title, the follower count. {trap}It can all be real and still come to nothing in the end.{/trap} {idea}The same effort with Allah in it becomes something that lasts.{/idea}
old: As long as I work hard, it all adds up.
new: Effort only lasts when it is built on faith.
try: Before your main task today, say Bismillah and set an intention for Allah.

title: They hated what Allah sent, so their deeds lost their worth.
subtitle: Dislike of revelation is the root
then: The verse names the reason behind the lost deeds. {trap}They disliked what Allah sent down.{/trap} {idea}The problem began in the heart, as a feeling toward revelation, before it showed in deeds.{/idea}
now: A verse comes up that asks something hard of you: about money, or a relationship, or your tongue. {trap}You feel a small flinch of dislike.{/trap} {idea}That flinch is worth noticing gently, not hiding.{/idea} Ask Allah to make you love what He sent.
old: My feelings about a verse do not matter if I mostly obey.
new: How my heart feels toward what Allah sent shapes the worth of everything I do.
try: Think of one Quranic teaching you resist. Ask Allah to help your heart accept it.

title: Walk the land and look at how others ended.
subtitle: History as a mirror
then: The verse asks those who denied the Prophet ﷺ to travel and look. Ibn Kathir says Allah punished the earlier nations for their denial {reward}and saved the believers among them.{/reward} {trap}A similar end awaits those who repeat it.{/trap}
now: You visit a museum or ruins on holiday and take photos. {idea}The verse asks for a different kind of looking: what did these people choose, and how did it end?{/idea} Then turn the question on your own habits.
old: History is about other people and other times.
new: The end of those before me is a mirror for my own choices.
try: Next time you read or watch any history, ask one question: what does this teach me?

title: Allah is our Protector, and you have none.
subtitle: The answer given at Uhud
then: Ibn Kathir recounts that after Uhud, Abu Sufyan boasted of his idols: {trap}we have al-Uzza and you have none.{/trap} The Prophet ﷺ told his companions to reply: {idea}Allah is our Protector, and you have no protector.{/idea} This verse says the same.
now: Someone mocks you: they have connections, money, a big family behind them, and you seem to have no one. {idea}Your reply does not need to be loud.{/idea} {reward}You have a Protector they cannot see.{/reward}
old: Without people or power behind me, I am unprotected.
new: Allah is the Protector of those who believe, whatever their numbers.
try: When you feel outnumbered today, say quietly: Allah is my Protector.

title: Eating like cattle, with no thought beyond the plate.
subtitle: Two ways to live, two places to end
then: Ibn Kathir says those who disbelieve {trap}eat like animals, munching with greed, with no concern beyond it.{/trap} He cites the Prophet ﷺ: {idea}a believer eats with one intestine, and a disbeliever with seven.{/idea}
now: Dinner in front of a screen, one more episode, a second plate you did not need. {trap}Life becomes intake.{/trap} {idea}The verse is not against food; it is against a life that is only about the next bite.{/idea}
old: Eating well and enjoying myself is all there is to a good life.
new: Enjoyment is fine, but a life with no aim beyond the plate is a life wasted.
try: At one meal today, eat without a screen and thank Allah before and after.

title: Stronger cities than the one that drove you out are gone.
subtitle: Comfort for the Prophet ﷺ who left Makkah
then: Ibn Abbas reported that at the cave during the Hijrah, the Prophet ﷺ looked back at Makkah and said {reward}you are the most beloved of Allah's lands to Allah and to me; had I not been driven out, I would never have left.{/reward} {idea}Allah then revealed that mightier towns had been destroyed, with none to help them.{/idea}
now: You had to leave a home, a job, a country, because of other people. You still miss it. {reward}The Prophet ﷺ loved the home he was forced from.{/reward} {idea}Loving a place is not weakness, and those who push you out do not have the last word.{/idea}
old: If I was pushed out, they won and my love for that place was foolish.
new: I can love what I lost and trust Allah with those who pushed me out.
try: If you miss a place you had to leave, make a short dua for it and its people.

title: Clear sight versus a life where wrong looks beautiful.
subtitle: The two people are not equal
then: Ibn Kathir describes the first person as {idea}on clear vision and certainty, through the Book and the pure nature Allah created him with.{/idea} The second has {trap}his bad deeds made to look beautiful, and follows his own lusts.{/trap} The two can never be equal.
now: A habit you know is wrong starts to look normal, even attractive, because everyone posts it. {trap}That is what made attractive feels like from the inside.{/trap} {idea}Clear evidence from your Lord is what lets you see it as it is.{/idea}
old: If something looks good and feels normal, it probably is fine.
new: Wrong can be made to look beautiful, so I need guidance to see clearly.
try: Name one thing that has started to look normal to you. Hold it up against one verse.

title: Four rivers that never spoil, and forgiveness on top.
subtitle: The description of Paradise promised to the mindful
then: Ibn Kathir says the water does not change or smell, the milk is pure and rich, the wine has no bad effect, and the honey is perfectly pure. The Prophet ﷺ said {reward}when you ask Allah, ask for al-Firdaws, the highest part, from which the rivers flow.{/reward} {idea}Above all of it is forgiveness from their Lord.{/idea}
now: Milk in your fridge goes off in a week. Your favorite treat gives you a stomachache. Everything here spoils a little. {reward}The verse describes good things that do not turn.{/reward} {idea}And it crowns them with forgiveness, the thing you most need.{/idea}
old: Every pleasure has a downside, so nothing can be fully good.
new: Allah has prepared good things that do not spoil, and forgiveness above them.
try: In your dua today, ask Allah by name for al-Firdaws.

title: Sitting in the gathering, then asking what was just said.
subtitle: Present in body, absent in heart
then: Ibn Kathir describes hypocrites who sat with the Prophet ﷺ and listened {trap}without understanding anything, nor caring.{/trap} Afterwards they asked the Companions what he had just said. {trap}Their hearts were sealed because they followed their desires.{/trap}
now: You sat through the whole Friday sermon. In the car someone asks what it was about, and you have no idea. You were planning your week. {idea}Being in the room is not the same as hearing.{/idea}
old: Showing up is the main thing.
new: Showing up matters, but my heart has to be there too to take anything away.
try: At the next talk or reminder you hear, write down one sentence from it afterwards.

title: Take one step toward guidance and more is given.
subtitle: Guidance grows for those who accept it
then: After the sealed hearts comes the opposite. Ibn Kathir says {reward}those who seek guidance, Allah makes it easy for them, guides them to it, makes them firm on it, and gives them more.{/reward} {idea}He also inspires them with their taqwa.{/idea}
now: You started with one short surah after Fajr. A month later you want to know what it means. Then you want to live it. {reward}That growth is the increase this verse promises.{/reward}
old: Guidance is something some people just have and others do not.
new: When I move toward guidance, Allah gives me more of it.
try: Take one small step toward learning your faith today: one verse, one meaning.

title: Waiting for the Hour, while its signs have already come.
subtitle: Remembering then will not help
then: Ibn Kathir says the coming of the Prophet ﷺ is itself one of the signs of the Hour, because he is the last Messenger ﷺ. Sahl bin Sa'd saw him join his index and middle fingers and say {idea}I have been sent before the Hour like these two.{/idea} {trap}When it comes, remembering will not help.{/trap}
now: You keep saying you will get serious about prayer after this busy month, after the wedding, after retirement. {trap}The verse says do not wait for a sudden ending to start remembering.{/trap} {idea}The signs are already here.{/idea}
old: There is plenty of time; I will get serious later.
new: The signs have already come, and remembering is only useful before the end.
try: Pick one thing you keep postponing for later in your faith and do a piece of it today.

title: Know there is no god but Allah, then ask forgiveness.
subtitle: Knowledge first, then forgiveness for you and others

row.title: everyone
sub: the Prophet ﷺ, 70 times a day

then: The command begins with knowing that there is no god but Allah. Then it joins that to seeking forgiveness for oneself and for all believers. Ibn Kathir records that the Prophet ﷺ said {idea}I ask Allah's forgiveness and repent to Him more than seventy times every day.{/idea} {reward}Allah knows your moving about and your place of rest.{/reward}
now: You make dua only for yourself and your family. {reward}This verse widens it: every believing man and woman.{/reward} The stranger on the bus, the doctor on night shift, the person who annoyed you in the queue.
old: Asking forgiveness is for when I have done something bad.
new: Seeking forgiveness is a daily habit, for me and for every believer.
try: Say astaghfirullah for yourself and for all believing men and women ten times today.

title: Asking for a hard command, then fainting when it comes.
subtitle: The gap between wishing and doing
then: The surah introduction says Madinah was tiny and surrounded. Ibn Kathir says believers hoped for a surah ordering them to fight. {trap}When it came, those with sickness in their hearts looked at the Prophet ﷺ like someone fainting at death.{/trap} {idea}The verse compares it to those who asked, then wanted it postponed.{/idea}
now: You say you would give anything for your parents. Then your mother needs a lift to the hospital at 6am and you groan. {trap}The wish was easy; the real ask shows where you are.{/trap}
old: I know I would do the hard thing if it were ever asked of me.
new: The test is not what I wish for but how I respond when it actually arrives.
try: Do one thing today you once said you would gladly do, now that it is actually asked.

title: Obedience and a good word would have been better.
subtitle: Being true when it becomes serious

key.label: What helps in a hard moment

then: After the fearful look comes gentle advice. Ibn Kathir says {idea}it would have been better for them to listen and obey in that situation.{/idea} When the matter became serious, {reward}being sincere to Allah would have been better for them.{/reward}
now: The family emergency, the hard diagnosis, the redundancy letter. You want to panic and complain to everyone. {idea}The verse offers a calmer path: obey, speak well, be sincere.{/idea} {reward}It is better for you, not only for Allah's cause.{/reward}
old: When things get serious, panic and complaint are only natural.
new: In serious moments, quiet obedience and good words serve me best.
try: The next time stress hits today, choose one good sentence to say instead of a complaint.

title: Turn away, and you go back to corruption and cutting family.
subtitle: What turning away really brings
then: Ibn Kathir says turning away would mean returning to the old ways of ignorance: bloodshed and cutting off relatives. He cites the Prophet ﷺ: {reward}the womb sought refuge in Allah from being cut, and Allah promised to join whoever joins it.{/reward} {idea}Joining ties is not dealing evenly, but reaching those who cut you off.{/idea}
now: There is an aunt you have not called in two years because she did not call you. A cousin muted in the family chat. {idea}Keeping score feels fair.{/idea} {reward}The verse and the hadith ask you to reach out first.{/reward}
old: I will keep in touch with relatives who keep in touch with me.
new: Keeping family ties means reaching out even to those who do not reach back.
try: Send one kind message today to a relative you have drifted away from.

title: Those who do this lose their hearing and their sight.
subtitle: Cutting ties dulls the heart
then: Ibn Kathir says this involves a general ban on spreading corruption and a specific one on cutting family ties. He cites the Prophet ﷺ: {trap}no sin more deserves to have its punishment hastened in this world than injustice and cutting kinship.{/trap} {reward}And whoever wants a longer life and more provision should join his ties.{/reward}
now: The family feud has gone on so long nobody remembers how it started. Everyone just avoids the other side at weddings. {idea}The verse says this is not small.{/idea} {reward}Mending it can open blessings you have not seen.{/reward}
old: A family feud is private and does not affect my faith.
new: Cutting off family is serious before Allah, and joining it brings real blessing.
try: Make dua tonight for one relative you are distant from, by name.

title: Do they not reflect, or are their hearts locked?
subtitle: The Quran is meant to be thought about
then: Ibn Kathir reports that when the Prophet ﷺ recited this, a young man from Yemen said {reward}there are locks on them, until Allah opens them, fully or a little.{/reward} Umar liked him for this and later made him an adviser. {idea}The verse commands reflection, not just recitation.{/idea}
now: You can finish a whole juz on your commute and not remember a single meaning. {idea}Speed is not the goal.{/idea} {reward}One verse you actually think about can open the lock a little.{/reward}
old: Reading more pages is the main way to benefit from the Quran.
new: Reflecting on even one verse matters more than racing through pages.
try: Read one verse slowly today, then sit for one minute with what it asks of you.

title: Turning back after it was clear, sold on false hopes.
subtitle: How Shaytan pulls someone away
then: This is about those who left faith after guidance had become clear. Ibn Kathir says Shaytan {trap}adorned it for them and filled them with false hopes, tempting and deceiving them.{/trap}
now: You drift from prayer slowly. A voice says: you are young, there is time, everyone does it, you will come back. {trap}That is the long false hope.{/trap} {idea}Notice the voice, and do not let it set your timetable.{/idea}
old: I have plenty of time to get back on track.
new: The feeling that there is always more time is one of Shaytan's oldest tools.
try: If you have been drifting, pray the next prayer on time, today, not later.

title: We will obey you in part, said in secret.
subtitle: Half-loyalty to those who hate the truth
then: Ibn Kathir says they {trap}plotted secretly with those who hated revelation and gave them evil advice{/trap}, as hypocrites show one thing and hide another. {idea}Allah knows whatever they hide.{/idea}
now: In one group chat you say all the right things. In another, you mock the same values to fit in. {trap}Just partly going along.{/trap} {idea}Allah sees both chats.{/idea}
old: What I say in private does not really count.
new: Allah knows my private words as clearly as my public ones.
try: Notice one place where you speak differently about your faith to fit in. Speak once as yourself.

title: How will it be when the angels come for them?
subtitle: The moment of death for those who turned back

row.title: a gentle end
sub: what I can still work for

then: After describing the hypocrites' secret deals, the verse asks a sober question. Ibn Kathir says {trap}their souls cling to their bodies, so the angels draw them out with force.{/trap} {idea}It is a reminder of how a life of double-dealing ends.{/idea}
now: Nobody chooses the day. It may be a hospital bed or a roadside. {idea}The only thing you shape is the person you are when it comes.{/idea} {reward}A heart at peace with Allah does not need to cling.{/reward}
old: I do not need to think about death until I am old.
new: How I live now shapes how I will meet the angels at the end.
try: Ask Allah today for a good ending, in your own words, once.

title: They chased what angers Him and disliked what pleases Him.
subtitle: The reason behind the hard ending
then: The verse explains the end described before it. {trap}They pursued what angered Allah and disliked what earns His pleasure, so He made their deeds worthless.{/trap} {idea}What a person loves and hates sets their direction.{/idea}
now: You notice you are bored by anything about Allah but alert for anything that pulls you away from Him. {idea}Desires have a direction.{/idea} {reward}You can ask Allah to turn your likes toward what pleases Him.{/reward}
old: What I like and dislike is just my personality.
new: My likes and dislikes point me toward or away from Allah's pleasure.
try: Make the dua: O Allah, make me love what You love. Say it three times today.

title: Did they think their hidden hatred would never show?
subtitle: What the heart hides comes out
then: Ibn Kathir says the hypocrites thought their ill-will would stay hidden. Allah later exposed their practices in Surah at-Tawbah, which is also called the Exposer. {idea}Uthman bin Affan said no one hides a secret but Allah shows it on his face and in slips of his tongue.{/idea}
now: You smile at your colleague's promotion while resenting it. It leaks out: a sharp comment, a pause too long. {trap}Envy rarely stays quiet.{/trap} {idea}Better to treat it than to hide it.{/idea}
old: If I keep my resentment private, it hurts no one.
new: Hidden ill-will tends to show, so I should heal it, not hide it.
try: Think of someone you quietly envy. Make a sincere dua for their good today.

title: You will know them by the tone of their speech.
subtitle: Allah conceals, but words reveal
then: Allah tells the Prophet ﷺ He could have shown him every hypocrite by name. Ibn Kathir says {idea}Allah did not, but conceals His creation, deals with them by what appears, and leaves inner secrets to Himself.{/idea} {trap}Still, their words reveal them.{/trap} And Allah knows all your deeds.
now: It is tempting to judge who at the mosque is sincere and who is not. {idea}The verse shows Allah's way: cover, go by what is visible, leave hearts to Him.{/idea} {reward}Then check your own tone, because Allah knows your deeds too.{/reward}
old: I can usually tell who is fake and should call them out.
new: Allah covers people, so I go by what I see and watch my own words.
try: Listen to your own tone in one conversation today. Does it match what you mean?

title: Tested until the striving and the patient are shown.
subtitle: Tests make the hidden visible
then: Allah says He will test the believers with commands and prohibitions. Ibn Kathir stresses {idea}His knowledge comes before every event{/idea}; Ibn Abbas said until We know means so that We may see. {reward}The tests make the striving and patient visible.{/reward}
now: The year with no job offers. The child who is always sick. The marriage going through a rough patch. {idea}It is not that Allah needs to find out who you are.{/idea} {reward}The test brings out your patience so it is seen and rewarded.{/reward}
old: If I am being tested, Allah must doubt me.
new: Tests bring out my striving and patience so they can be seen and rewarded.
try: Name your current test and say: this is where my patience gets shown. Then do one patient act.

title: Opposing the truth harms only yourself, never Allah.
subtitle: Turning back after guidance was clear
then: Ibn Kathir says those who opposed the Messenger ﷺ after guidance was clear {idea}could never harm Allah in the least; they only harmed themselves.{/idea} {trap}Even good they did before turning back would bring them no reward.{/trap}
now: You argue with a truth because it is inconvenient: you mock it, block it, refuse it. {idea}The truth does not shrink.{/idea} {trap}The only thing that shrinks is what you gain from it.{/trap}
old: If I push back hard enough, I can make the truth go away.
new: Fighting the truth cannot harm Allah; it only costs me.
try: Think of one truth you resist. Stop arguing with it for one day and see what changes.

title: Obey, and do not cancel out your own deeds.
subtitle: The verse that made the Companions careful
then: Ibn Umar said the Companions {trap}used to think all good deeds would be accepted{/trap} until this was revealed. They began to fear that some sins could cancel deeds. Later, after verse 4:48, {idea}they kept fearing for those who committed great sins and hoping for those who did not.{/idea}
now: You worked hard all Ramadan, then spent the next month on backbiting and anger. {idea}Good deeds are like savings: you can earn them, and you can also spend them away.{/idea} {reward}Guard what you built.{/reward}
old: Once I have done good deeds, they are safe forever.
new: My deeds are worth guarding, so I keep both fear and hope.
try: Pick one good deed you are proud of. Protect it today by avoiding one habit that undoes it.

title: Dying on rejection closes the door to forgiveness.
subtitle: The one thing that ends hope
then: Ibn Kathir links this verse to 4:48, that Allah does not forgive joining partners with Him. {trap}The key word is died: they died as disbelievers.{/trap} {reward}While a person is alive, the way back stays open.{/reward}
now: You think it is too late for you, or for someone you love who has strayed. {reward}The verse quietly says the opposite: while there is breath, the door is open.{/reward} {idea}The only deadline is the last one.{/idea}
old: Some people, maybe me, are too far gone to come back.
new: As long as I am alive, the way back to Allah is open.
try: Make a dua today for someone you have given up on, that Allah guides them.

title: Do not lose heart: Allah is with you.
subtitle: Strength for a small, pressed community
then: Ibn Kathir says this tells the believers not to be weak and seek a truce out of fear while they hold the upper hand. He notes that when it served the Muslims, {idea}the Prophet ﷺ accepted a ten-year treaty after being blocked from Makkah.{/idea} {reward}Allah is with you and will never reduce your deeds.{/reward}
now: You are close to finishing the degree, the memorization, the long repair of a friendship, and you want to quit. {idea}Not every pause is weakness, but quitting from fear when you can carry on often is.{/idea} {reward}Allah is with you, and no effort is lost.{/reward}
old: When it gets hard, it is easier to just give up.
new: With Allah with me, I do not need to give up from fear, and none of my effort is lost.
try: Do one more small step today on something you have been tempted to abandon.

title: This life is play, and He does not ask all you own.
subtitle: What lasts, and what is actually asked
then: Ibn Kathir says this life is only play, except what is done for Allah. {idea}He needs nothing from you.{/idea} {reward}He asked for charity so you would help your needy brothers, and its benefit and reward come back to you.{/reward}
now: Your weekend disappears into scrolling and shopping, and on Monday you cannot remember any of it. {idea}That is the play and distraction.{/idea} {reward}The hour you spent helping a neighbor move is the part that stays.{/reward}
old: Giving charity is a cost that takes from me.
new: Allah does not need my money; giving helps others and comes back to me.
try: Give a small amount to someone in need today, and notice how it feels.

title: If He pressed you for everything, you would hold back.
subtitle: Allah knows how attached we are to money
then: Ibn Kathir quotes Qatadah: {idea}Allah knows that taking people's money brings out ill-will.{/idea} He adds that Qatadah was right, {trap}because money is dear to people, and they only spend it on what is dearer to them.{/trap} So Allah asks for a part, not all.
now: Someone asks to borrow a large sum and you feel a tightness in your chest. {idea}That tightness is human, and Allah knows it.{/idea} {reward}It is why He asks for a portion, not everything.{/reward}
old: I would give anything for Allah if He asked.
new: Allah knows how much I cling to money, so He asks only a portion with mercy.
try: Notice the tight feeling the next time you spend on someone else, and give anyway.

title: Whoever holds back is only holding back from himself.
subtitle: Allah is free of need, and we are the needy
then: The believers were invited to spend in Allah's cause, and some held back. Ibn Kathir says {trap}the stingy person only reduces his own reward.{/trap} {idea}Allah needs nothing, while everything needs Him.{/idea} If they turned away, He would bring people who would obey.
now: A fundraiser link sits unopened in your messages. You tell yourself someone else will cover it. {idea}Someone probably will.{/idea} {trap}The only one who loses out is you.{/trap}
old: If I do not give, the cause loses out.
new: Allah's work will go on; if I hold back, I am the one who loses.
try: Open one charity request you have been ignoring and give something, however small.
